SEB's own pre-close steers put NII and NFI below a FactSet bar that still has NII +257m q/q, in a week when Handelsbanken and Nordea were sold 3-8% on NII shortfalls, and the first capital-return statement after FI's IRB decision cannot carry a buyback.

Norcros flagged softer UK bathroom demand across exactly Svedbergs' Q3 after both broker previews were written, an undisclosed Dalstorp restructuring charge lands below the adjusted line, and the two previews disagree by 10% with the higher one at risk.

An unreleased Delaware Supreme Court ruling adding ~USD 8.5m to the indemnity and removing the appeal tail, Fidelio buying SEK 390m days before the closed period, and Virbac's companion-animal beat outweigh a segment build ~0.5-1pp light on organic growth and a cash-conversion question.

TTF gas at 59-72 EUR/MWh through Q3 against 31-35 a year earlier, with management already at the low end of the EBITDA guide and no downgrade in the market, raises the risk of a guide trim like Q3 2025's; the FX tailwind and ~2.3% disclosed short only soften it.
